Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Javanese ꦕꦺꦴꦫꦺꦴ (coro, “cockroach”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃoro/ [ˈt͡ʃo.ro]
  • Rhymes: -oro
  • Syllabification: co‧ro

Noun

[edit]

coro (plural coro-coro)

  1. (colloquial, dialectal) synonym of kecoak (“cockroach”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “coro”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

  • Rhymes: -ɔro
  • Hyphenation: cò‧ro

Noun

[edit]

coro m (plural cori)

  1. chorus
  2. choir

Related terms

[edit]
  • corale

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Orco, orco, roco

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
coro
Wikipedia pt

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese coro, probably borrowed from Latin chorus, from Ancient Greek χορός (khorós). Doublet of chorus.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • côro (obsolete)

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈko.ɾu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈko.ɾu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈko.ɾo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈko.ɾu/

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -oɾu
  • Homophone: couro
  • Hyphenation: co‧ro

Noun

[edit]

coro m (plural coros, metaphonic)

  1. (collective) choir (singing group)
    Eu canto num coro. ― I sing in a choir.
  2. (architecture) choir (part of a church or concert hall where the choir assembles)
Usage notes
[edit]

The plural may be pronounced with either /o/ or /ɔ/.

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkɔ.ɾu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkɔ.ɾu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkɔ.ɾo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈkɔ.ɾu/

  • Rhymes: -ɔɾu
  • Hyphenation: co‧ro

Verb

[edit]

coro

  1. first-person singular present indicative of corar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “coro”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “coro”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish coro, borrowed from Latin chorus, from Ancient Greek χορός (khorós).[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈkoɾo/ [ˈko.ɾo]
  • Rhymes: -oɾo
  • Syllabification: co‧ro

Noun

[edit]

coro m (plural coros)

  1. choir
    Canto en un coro
    I sing in a choir
  2. (music) chorus (of a song)
    ¡Amo el coro de esta canción!
    I love the chorus in this song!
  3. (architecture) choir (area where singers in a church stand)
    El coro de la iglesia necesita reparaciones o sino se desplomará.
    The church choir needs repairs or else it'll collapse.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • a coro
  • capa de coro
  • capellán de coro
  • infante de coro
  • libro de coro
  • niño de coro
  • rezar a coros
  • sotacoro

Related terms

[edit]
  • coral

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Coromines, Joan; Pascual, José Antonio (1983–1991), “coro”, in Diccionario crítico etimológico castellano e hispánico [Critical Castilian and Hispanic etymological dictionary]‎[1] (in Spanish), Madrid: Gredos

Further reading

[edit]
